claims.text: A fitness function is an automated check that the system still has a quality attribute it must keep, run with every change instead of left to people's memory.

claims.text: The image job builds the images, writes an SBOM of each (Syft), then the Grype step (ci.yml line 140 calls scan-image.sh) fails on a High or Critical vulnerability with a fixed version unless .grype.yaml accepts it; pass: images saved; fail: run stops first.
Quality attributes and their decisions are recorded in ADRs; a fitness function does not decide the attribute, it makes later changes keep it.

ServiceUsesNoDonHangProjectButMessaging runs once per InlineData type (OrderEventsConsumer in Notifications, RefundRequestedConsumer in Payments), keeps referenced names starting with DonHang. other than DonHang.Messaging (line 66) and asserts the list is empty (line 69).
DependencyRuleTests.DomainReferencesNoOuterAssembly fails when DonHang.Domain references a name starting with a prefix in ForbiddenPrefixes, which at stage-3 includes DonHang.Catalog and RabbitMQ.

OrdersApiTests checks feature behaviour, e.g. PostOrder_SignedInCustomer_Returns201WithLocation asserts 201 and a Location header; ModuleBoundaryTests checks project dependencies independently of feature behaviour.
A service opening its own database connection (connection string, Npgsql) to another service's database adds no DonHang.* assembly reference, so ModuleBoundaryTests still passes.

.grype.yaml at stage-3 accepts one vulnerability, CVE-2024-10041: a Medium PAM flaw with no fix (so --only-fixed --fail-on high would not fail on it); PAM is what a program uses to authenticate a user; the images run one dotnet process and no login.

claims.text: Trade-offs: a person in review sees intent but only when they link the change to the decision; a test in the test project runs on every change but sees only what it reads; a separate tool sees only what its data knows. Fitness functions suit what can be stated exactly.

claims.text: When an ADR secures a new separation, write its fitness function in the first pull request whose code already obeys it (at once if nothing crosses yet, else when the last crossing goes). On a fixable Grype finding prefer the fix; accept in .grype.yaml only with a reason, remove when untrue.

ADR 0002 secured that Notifications does not read the API's tables (the message carries the customer's email and name); no current check states this, so it should be named unguarded and watched by a reviewer.
